title: Streams run in the engine: incidents as a related table, the holdout cut from dates, the alert method chosen on validation
request: Phase C of 16.15, second part: run the streams kind (machine readings, rare incidents, alerts within a budget) through the engine's five stages, the incidents a related table of the project, the holdout locked from dates, the method and threshold chosen on validation and the holdout read once.
spec: The streams library split into split, known_by, training_view, choose and score; the kind's machine per stage; the incidents attached as a related table; the engine acceptance on the machine replica.
plan: Split streams.evaluate into what each stage runs, keeping evaluate for the library acceptance.
Write the kind's engine fields, solution checks and machine.
Test that the holdout's readings and incidents reach only the final stage.

decisions.decision: Training reads the readings before the cut and only the incidents known by it, their label delay included.
decisions.why: An incident whose label arrives after the cut cannot have been known when the model was built.

decisions.decision: The cut is placed on the time axis, not by counting windows.
decisions.why: Machines stop reporting while down after a failure, so counting windows lets the holdout's failures move the line.

decisions.decision: A sensor that follows the hours to the next failure far before it is kept out until a person confirms it.
decisions.why: A back-filled column is written in the past but knows the future; time checks cannot see it.

decisions.decision: With no incident to score on validation, the choice is refused rather than made by a tie-break.
decisions.why: A method reported as chosen by incident recall must have been chosen by it.

change: dclab_core/streams.py (split, known_by, training_view, choose, score, written_ahead, without, wilson; dclab-core 0.26.0), dclab_rnd/kinds/streams.py (fields, checks, StreamMachine, engine acceptance; the incidents in Case.tables); tests/test_core_streams.py, tests/test_kind_acceptance_streams.py (new); CHANGELOG, the playbook, the roadmap.

findings.defect: Reading incidents not yet known by the cut went unnoticed.
findings.scenario: A planted fault dropped the label-delay filter and every test passed.
findings.cause: With the replica's zero delay the filter changes nothing; no test asked it directly.
findings.fix: A test checks the incidents known by the cut with a 72-hour delay.

findings.defect: Fitting on the machines left out for the unseen-machine measure went unnoticed.
findings.scenario: A planted fault fitted on every machine and every test passed.
findings.cause: The record did not say which machines the measure was fitted on.
findings.fix: The record lists the machines fitted on; a test checks they never meet the ones left out.

findings.defect: With no incident in the validation period the method was chosen by a tie-break and reported as chosen by incident recall.
findings.scenario: Dropping the incidents of the validation period left every recall empty and own_change chosen on false alerts 0.200 against 0.202.
findings.cause: Only the incidents before the validation period were counted.
findings.fix: choose refuses a validation period with no scoreable incident.

findings.defect: A sensor filled in knowing when the failure came was used unflagged.
findings.scenario: A service counter of hours to the next failure, capped at 300, moved no window and was chosen with validation recall 1.0.
findings.cause: The leakage stage only listed columns not read; time checks cannot see a back-filled value.
findings.fix: written_ahead flags sensors following the hours to the next incident far before it (Spearman 0.87 for the counter); they are kept out until confirmed.

findings.defect: With no holdout incident the gap reported a drop that never happened.
findings.scenario: Holdout recall None was taken as 0 and the gap reported as minus the validation recall.
findings.cause: A missing value replaced by zero.
findings.fix: The gap is None when either side is; the claim says no holdout incident can be scored.

findings.defect: The unseen-machine refit could crash after the holdout was read.
findings.scenario: With no validation window left on the other machines, scikit-learn raised on an empty array in the final stage.
findings.cause: The library's evaluate guarded the refit; score did not.
findings.fix: The measure is left empty, and said, when the others have no validation window.

findings.defect: Failures after the cut moved the cut.
findings.scenario: One more day of downtime per machine after the cut moved it from 06:00 to 00:00 and the validation start by a step.
findings.cause: The cut was a quantile of window ends, and downtime writes fewer windows.
findings.fix: The cut and the validation start are placed on the time axis.

findings.scenario: 22 of 22 incidents were reported without an interval.
findings.fix: A Wilson 95% interval: 0.85 to 1.0 for 22 of 22.

findings.defect: The capability matrix was not rebuilt.
findings.scenario: The matrix still showed streams as partial.
findings.cause: The campaign needs the committed code.
findings.fix: The campaign and kinds-check run after the code commit.

measurements.name: the machine replica in the engine, seed 0
measurements.gate: every engine acceptance decision holds: no window reads past the cut, the method chosen on validation is scored once, at least 0.75 incident recall with 6 hours of warning within 1.5 times the budget, machines never seen scored
measurements.result: 12 of 12 decisions hold: supervised chosen; 22 of 22 holdout incidents caught (95% 0.85 to 1.0), median 36.0 hours before, 0.232 alerts per machine-day against a budget of 0.2; 9 of 9 incidents on unseen machines; 0 of 2782 windows moved
limits: 22 incidents: recall read on few events.
How long after an incident starts it is detected is not measured.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each planted fault fails a test
measurements.result: 15 of 15 planted faults caught after the fixes

outcome: Streams run in the engine: readings as the table and incidents as a related table, the holdout cut on the time axis, training from what was known by then, back-filled sensors kept out until confirmed, the method and threshold chosen on validation, the holdout scored once with an interval.
lessons: A split read off counts of rows can move with the outcome when outcomes change how many rows exist; place it on the time axis.
A value written in the past can still know the future: test what a column follows far from the event, not only when it was written.
A choice that cannot be made by its rule must be refused, not made by the tie-break.
risks: Embedded data is still outside the engine.
The written-ahead check reads one shape (a value following the hours left); other back-filled shapes may pass.
